evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/QRCodeScanner.ts exports parseQRCode (line 29), getQRCodeAction (line 247) and provideScanFeedback (line 333); QRCodeGenerator.ts exports the generator — all tagged 'Epic 49 - Story 49.3: QR Code Scanning'. An app-wide grep (excluding the qrcode/ dir itself and *.test.*) finds ZERO consumers of parseQRCode / getQRCodeAction / QRCodeGenerator / provideScanFeedback anywhere in frontend/apps/mobile/src. The parse+action library is dead code from the app's perspective.

There is NO camera/scanner capability wired in: a grep for expo-camera / expo-barcode-scanner / BarCodeScanner / CameraView / useCameraPermissions across src returns nothing, and frontend/apps/mobile/package.json declares no camera|barcode|scanner|vision dependency. So even though the parsing logic exists, the app physically cannot scan a QR code — there is no scanner screen and no camera module. Story 49.3's user-facing capability is unimplemented despite the supporting library being present (a feature that looks shipped by file presence but is not reachable).

Contrast confirms this is a genuine omission, not a static-analysis artifact: the sibling module qrcode/DeepLinkHandler.ts IS wired at runtime (consumed via hooks/useDeepLinkRouting.ts -> App.tsx, and Linking.addEventListener), so the unused-ness of the scanner/generator is specific, not a whole-dir quirk. Secondary latent concern for when it is eventually wired: getQRCodeAction's external_url branch (QRCodeScanner.ts:314-319) returns {action:'open_url'} for ANY http(s) URL with only a textual confirmation string and no host allowlist/scheme hardening — a scanned malicious QR would map straight to an open-URL action once a consumer exists. Suggested vector: either wire a camera scanner screen (add expo-camera, build the scan UI, consume parseQRCode + enforce getQRCodeAction confirmations with a host allowlist) or remove the dead qrcode scan/generate library and mark Story 49.3 incomplete.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/voice/ ships VoiceAssistant.ts and VoiceCommands.ts (plus types.ts, index.ts, VoiceCommands.i18n.test.ts). An app-wide grep for VoiceAssistant / VoiceCommands (excluding the voice/ dir and *.test.*) finds ZERO consumers across frontend/apps/mobile/src — no screen, navigation entry, or App.tsx imports the voice module.

This is a cross-stack completeness gap, not merely dead FE code: the backend implements the counterpart service at backend/servers/api-server/src/services/voice_commands.rs (VoiceCommandProcessor: parse_command, process_command, action_report_fault/check_balance/check_meter/etc., persisted via llm_document_repo.create_voice_command). So the server side of voice assistant is built and RLS-scoped, but the mobile client that would drive it is present-yet-unwired — the feature cannot be exercised end-to-end from the app.

Impact low-medium: no runtime crash (the module simply never runs), but a built feature library with a live backend is silently inert, which both misrepresents delivery status and risks bit-rot. Confidence medium: verified no static consumer via app-wide grep; RN does not use dynamic require for these modules. Suggested vector: either wire the voice entry point (a screen/button that instantiates VoiceAssistant and calls the /voice backend) or explicitly defer and mark the mobile voice story incomplete so the backend endpoint isn't left as an untested surface.
